newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast to privatise road maintenance.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast to privatise road maintenance.

text.p: Ivory Coast plans to privatise road maintenance in an attempt to halt the deterioration of the infrastructure and cater for future traffic growth, officials told a seminar here this week.

"Privatisation will do a lot of good because the government lacks financial resources. We cannot do much when we are asked to do something about broken bridges or when roads are cut off," said the country's director of roads, Desire Gnonkonte.

Roads deteriorated badly when the Ivory Coast economy was depressed between 1990 and 1993, and minister of economic infrastructure Ezan Akele said some 40 billion CFA francs ($80 million) per year was needed for maintenance.
Ivory Coast is reckoned to have one of the best road systems in sub-Saharan Africa, with some 5,800 km (3,500 miles) of its 70,000 km (45,000 miles) of roads having hard surfaces.
Following the degradation of the early 1990s, the government invested 270 billion CFA francs in maintenance.
But a study carried out under the country's Road and Rehabilitation Project showed that 45 percent of roads were in a bad state, 35 percent were average and only 20 percent were reckoned to be good.
As a result, the country nows needs 40 billion CFA francs per year for maintenance, officials said.
Ivory Coast will be looking for assistance from institutions like the World Bank and the European Commissiom that sponsored the seminar.
Ivory Coast has ambitious growth plans, and better road infrastructure is central to these ambitions.
"Roads, in general, are a powerful factor of social and economic progress," Akele said.
"Building roads is something very expensive for developing countries," roads director Gnonkonte said. "One kilometre of road surfaced with tarmac costs about 120 million CFA francs ($240,000)."
